unit.title: CSS: text and colors
unit.description: Text color, background color, font size and weight, alignment, hex color codes, comments

cards.definition: The property that paints the letters of an element, not the box behind them.
cards.example: button { color: white; } makes the label of every button white.

cards.definition: Fills the box behind the content of an element with a color.
cards.example: body { background-color: #f5f5f5; } gives the whole page a light gray backdrop.

cards.definition: Sets how big the letters are, usually in pixels (px) or in rem.
cards.example: h1 { font-size: 32px; } makes main headings twice the usual 16px.

cards.definition: Sets how thick the letters are: normal, bold, or a number from 100 (thin) to 900 (very heavy).
cards.example: Bold is the same as 700; normal is 400.

cards.definition: Places the lines inside their box: left, right, center or justify.
cards.example: h1 { text-align: center; } centers the main heading.

cards.definition: A color written as # and six characters: two for red, two for green, two for blue, each from 00 to ff.
A note written between /* and */ that the browser skips; it explains the code to humans.
cards.example: /* Main button */ above a rule says what it styles.

exercises.prompt: Which property changes the color of the TEXT?
exercises.explain: The text color is simply color. The box behind the text has its own property: background-color.
whyWrong: background-color paints behind the text, not the letters.
text-color does not exist: the browser ignores it.
font-color does not exist in CSS.

exercises.prompt: What does this button look like?
choices: White text on a navy background
Navy text on a white background
exercises.explain: color paints the letters (white), background-color fills the box behind them (navy).
whyWrong: It is the other way round: color is the text, background-color the box.
color: white sets the text; navy is used for the background.
background-color: navy does fill the background.

exercises.prompt: Which declaration makes a heading bigger?
exercises.explain: font-size sets the size of the letters. px means pixels: 16px is the usual size of body text.
whyWrong: font-weight sets how thick the letters are, not their size.
text-size does not exist in CSS.
size is not a property for text.

exercises.prompt: How do you center the text of a heading?
exercises.explain: text-align places the lines inside their box: left, right, center or justify.
whyWrong: align alone is not a CSS property.
middle is not a valid value here: write center.
CSS has no property called center.

exercises.explain: font-weight controls how thick the letters are: normal (400) or bold (700).
whyWrong: font-style is used for italic, not bold.
text-weight does not exist in CSS.
font-size expects a size, such as 20px.

exercises.explain: In a hex code, 00 means none of that light. No red, no green, no blue: black.
whyWrong: White is #ffffff: every pair at its maximum.
Red is #ff0000: only the first pair is high.
A gray has three equal middle pairs, like #808080.

exercises.prompt: color: red; and color: #ff0000; give the same red.
exercises.explain: red is a color name, #ff0000 is the same red written in hex: full red, no green, no blue.

exercises.prompt: Build a declaration that sets the size of the text to 20 pixels.
exercises.explain: font-size: 20px; is the property, a colon, the value with its unit, then a semicolon. Without px, the browser ignores the size.

exercises.prompt: The heading is not centered. Which line is wrong?
exercises.explain: CSS uses the American spelling: center, not centre. An unknown value makes the browser skip that declaration.

exercises.prompt: What does the browser do with the first line?
choices: Nothing: it is a note for humans
It shows it above the heading
exercises.explain: Everything between /* and */ is a comment: the browser skips it. Comments explain your code to the next reader.
whyWrong: Comments are never shown on the page.
A comment changes nothing on the page.
Comments are valid CSS, so there is no error.

exercises.prompt: The same property appears twice. What color is the text?
choices: A mix of red and green
exercises.explain: When a property is repeated, the declaration written last wins. CSS is read from top to bottom.
whyWrong: Red comes first, then the line below replaces it.
CSS never mixes two colors: one value wins.
Repeating a property is allowed: the last one wins.

exercises.prompt: Build a rule that centers the text of every h2 heading.
exercises.explain: h2 { text-align: center; } text-align places the lines of text; center puts them in the middle.

exercises.prompt: Build a rule that gives the body a light gray background (#eeeeee).
exercises.explain: body { background-color: #eeeeee; } A hex color starts with #, followed by six characters.
